fields.Name: MfgDate
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Factories often have shift schedules that result in a shift starting work on one date and ending on another date; where 12 midnight is in the middle of the shift.  For these factories, it is normal to have a concept of "Manufacturing Date" that enables any particular shift to fall entirely on one particular manufacturing day.  A factory with shifts that start at 7am, 3pm, and 11pm will normally have a "Manufacturing Date" that begins on 11pm of the previous clock date, and ends at 11pm of the current clock date.

fields.Name: MfgProcessOverrides
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Bill Of Process is used to specify overrides to a specification (spec), and is assigned to a container, manufacturing order or a product.

fields.Name: Operation
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Operation where the transaction took place.

fields.Name: Owner
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Every Container has an associated Owner Code. The owner code is used as a grouping to separate Containers for inquiry and processing. Examples of Owner Code are "Manufacturing", "Engineering", "Prototypes", "SalesSamples", etc.

fields.Name: Product
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations:
An instance of a Product Definition describes a product to the application. This may be a Product to be manufactured, raw materials, finished, etc. Products can belong to a Product Family. A product to be manufactured will have an associated Workflow. Attributes of the Workflow may be overridden to be product specific.

Optionally, a Product can belong to a Product Family. A Product Family is used to group products for the purpose of simplifying the maintenance task (for modeling data). Common attributes such as costing or processing information can then be provided for a Product Family and applied to each Product within the family.

fields.Name: QualityESigConfirmed
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: The flag indicates is the Txn confirmed by the Quality Electronic Signature

fields.Name: RemainingProcessTime
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Remaining Process Time value, used for RPT calculation.

fields.Name: Resource
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Resource where the transaction took place.

fields.Name: ResourceAvailability
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations:
Defines the current availability status for a Resource.
Valid values and their meanings are:

1 = Up (Available)
2 = Down (Not available)

fields.Name: ResourceStatusCode
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations:
A Resource Status Code is provides a description of the current availability for a Resource. This value is used for inquiry and in reporting. (Mean Time Between Failure, Mean Time to Repair, Time at Status, etc.).

Additionally, a Resource Status code identifies the default “Next” (Production) Transaction for a Resource. This is intended to be a simple implementation of a Resource Status Flow (Resource Workflow).

fields.Name: ResourceStatusReason
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: A Resource Status Reason Code is used to provide an added level of detail describing the reason for the current status of a Resource. For example, the current status may be REPAIR. A Status Reason Code can be used to provide additional details such as the type of repair that is being performed. This detail is included in the transaction history, which makes it available for Analysis Reporting.

fields.Name: ReversalStatus
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations:
The status of this record in relation to Transaction Reversal.
Values are: 
1 = "Active" A non-reversed transaction has been executed. The ReversalStatus is initially set to this value for all committed transactions.

2 = "Deleted" A reversal transaction has been executed. Once a  transaction has been reversed, it's original HistoryMainline record is preserved, but the "ReversalStatus" is changed to deleted.

3 = "Reversal" A reversal transaction has been executed. A new HistoryMainline record is created for each "deleted" transaction. The data of the new HistoryMainline is based on the original transaction data, but the ReversalStatus is set to "Reversal". The User and DateTime stamp reflect the details of the ContainerTxnRev service. New copies of the corresponding history summaries and history details are created for the reversed transaction. Fields (such as the quantity fields in the history detail) are negated that have the flag "Txn Reversal-Compensate" checked on the Properties advanced tab. The "deleted" record will have a positive quantity, and the "reversal" record will have a negative quantity, and when summed (ie:reporting), the total will be zero.

fields.Name: Server
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Unique identifier of the Server that processed the transaction.

fields.Name: ShiftName
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Typically applies to manufacturing companies that have areas staffed for a long enough during a day that workers do not all start and end their day at the same time.  Shift is a mechanism for grouping production information based on management responsibilities for workers that start and leave at a particular time.  For example, the "Day" shift might work from 6am to 6pm, and the "Night" shift would work from 6pm to 6am.

fields.Name: Spec
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations:
A specification (Spec) describes the processing that takes place at a Step within a Workflow. It references many other Modeling components including an Operation, Setup, Data Collection Definitions and Resources. Specs also include detailed scheduling and processing parameter information. A Spec is referenced (used) by a Step within a Workflow. Many Workflow Steps can use one Spec.

A Spec is used to define the processing that is to be performed. An Operation is used to define (rules for) the flow or movement of Material through the Factory.

See the Operation Definition for Scheduling Details information.

fields.Name: Status
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations:
Determines the current status (Active, In-Active) of this instance. Valid values and their meanings are:

1 = Active
2 = Inactive

fields.Name: StepPass
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: The number of times the Container has passed through this Step.

fields.Name: SystemDate
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: The date and time that this transaction was recorded.

fields.Name: SystemDateGMT
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: The date and time that this transaction was recorded.

fields.Name: TxnDate
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: The date and time the work represented by this transaction was performed.

fields.Name: TxnDateGMT
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: The date and time the work represented by this transaction was performed.

fields.Name: TxnServiceName
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: The name of the service and is stored in History Mainline for shop floor services

fields.Name: TxnServiceSequence
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Stores the sequence of services being executed within a transaction. In a compound transaction or container transactions that calls other container transactions, multiple services may be called. Since all of them are having the same TxnId and TxnDate, this field is then used to indicate the sequence of services being executed.

fields.Name: TxnType
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Transaction type.  Returns "MyMove" as opposed to "Move".

fields.Name: User
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Identifies the person who recorded the transaction.

fields.Name: WorkflowStep
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: Workflow Step where the transaction took place (or started, i.e. <From> step is written for transactions like <Move>).

fields.Name: Workstation
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations:
A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.

A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.

fields.Name: ComputationHistory
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: History of the Computation

fields.Name: HistoryDetails

fields.Name: ParametricDetail
fields.{customAttribute}Annotations: ParametricDetail

fields.Name: WIPMsgHistoryDetails

fields.Name: Vendor

A vendor is a provider of goods and services. An example of these goods and services are components and subassemblies used to manufacture products, products purchased for resale, non-production materials,
services such as resource and building maintenance and so on.

Fields (such as the quantity fields in the history detail) are negated that have the flag "Txn Reversal-Compensate" checked on the Properties advanced tab. The "deleted" record will have a positive quantity, and the "reversal" record will have a negative quantity, and when summed (ie:reporting), the total will be zero.

A Resource describes any non-material entity within a factory. The common use (and most concrete example) of a Resource is to describe a Machine. Resources are associated with a single factory, to define their physical location. Resources also belong to zero or more Resource Groups, to provide a logical grouping.

A Resource is a static (modeling) entity. Each Resource can have a Resource Status entry to track the current status for each Status Category defined. The application is delivered with three specific Status Categories. They are Production, Preventative Maintenance and Log. Production is used to determine availability for production. Preventative Maintenance is used to track the current Preventative Maintenance status for a Resource. Log is used to provide a mechanism for logging freeform comments and optionally assigning predefined status and reason codes. Customers can define additional Status categories to concurrently track Resource status is multiple user-defined ways.
